_lock_notice: This file is committed BEFORE any evaluation checked against it is run, per the execution plan's discipline point on tolerances/eval-sets. Do not edit the numeric values below after generation/validation has been run once against a given generator_version -- bump generator_version instead and re-lock a new file. See PHASE2_NOTES.md 'Locked-before-use' section for the exact run order this was honored in.

ground_truth_treatment_effect.description: Empirical treatment effect (mean recovered-amount-fraction for a candidate bucket minus mean recovered-amount-fraction for do_nothing, same cases) must agree with the analytic effect implied by the generator's own z/p function, within this tolerance, per bucket aggregated across all cases and candidates in that bucket.
ground_truth_treatment_effect._amendment_reason: The ORIGINAL bucket definition (action_type alone) pooled candidates across root causes with opposite-signed analytic effects into one 'retry' bucket -- e.g. gateway_timeout/network_error pull positive, insufficient_funds/authentication_failed/expired_card (same-method) pull negative -- netting a true effect near zero, whose EMPIRICAL SIGN is then dominated by sampling noise regardless of dataset size. This was diagnosed with real evidence, not assumed: identical seed=42 runs on two independent machines (Linux build environment and the user's own Windows machine) reproduced the exact same instability to float64 precision, and a per-root-cause breakdown showed the mechanism directly -- this is the 'explained first, independently of the specific failing result' bar the task's own discipline requires before changing anything post-hoc. Implementing the fix also surfaced a SECOND, independent bug: the original merge only joined on (case_id, candidate_action), which silently many-to-many joined every case with more than one candidate sharing an action_type (e.g. multiple retry timing/method combinations) -- fixed by merging on the full candidate identity (case_id + action + timing + method + channel), asserted to be a strict 1:1 join. Bucketing itself is now by a PROVABLY-MINIMAL root-cause effect_class (transient / insufficient_funds / needs_action / payment_declined), derived directly from outcome_model.py's action_effectiveness() and timing_term() -- the only two functions that branch on root_cause at all -- rather than raw root_cause, since e.g. escalate's analytic effect is root-cause-independent for every payment_failed case and splitting it by raw root_cause manufactured spurious mismatches with no real underlying distinction to detect. Per the same discipline as before: max_absolute_probability_gap, min_fraction_of_buckets_matching_direction, and min_cases_per_bucket_for_check remain UNCHANGED from their original 2026-08-30T15:32:43Z lock -- only the bucket definition and the merge-key bug were touched.

reproducibility.description: Identical seed + calibration_profile + generator_version must produce byte-identical joint-dataset and truth-dataset CSV output on a second run. No numeric tolerance -- this is an exact-match check.

calibration_profile_divergence.description: Two named profiles must differ materially, not just by seed -- checked as a minimum relative difference in mean bank_health_score and mean overall recovery rate between baseline and stress, generated from the SAME seed.

unseen_eval_split.description: The temporal holdout reserved for Phase 3's cross-profile and temporal generalization gates. Locked here as a boundary on sim_hour, not chosen after seeing Phase 3 results -- Phase 3 must treat sim_hour >= this fraction of the horizon, for the baseline-profile dataset, as unseen at model-selection time.

fatigue_significance._lock_notice: Added after Phase 2's first review round, in response to the Phase Acceptance Test Gates' tightened fatigue gate. This sub-block is committed BEFORE fatigue_significance_check() was ever run against real data -- the only run against these numbers is the one in the current PHASE2_NOTES.md addendum, and it postdates this timestamp.
fatigue_significance.description: Named statistic: Pearson correlation between prior_contacts_in_window and recovered, computed on contact-type candidates (reminder/payment_link/escalate/retry, excluding do_nothing since fatigue has no defined effect there). Expected sign is negative (more prior contact -> lower recovery). Two-sided p-value from scipy.stats.pearsonr.

eval_set_lock._lock_notice: This policy block was already present (see unseen_eval_split above) but was not, until now, backed by an actual generated+hashed artifact. eval_set_lock.py's first-ever run against this policy postdates this timestamp.

phase3_data_split.description: 4-way, case-disjoint AND customer-disjoint split of the baseline-profile seed-42 joint dataset (Decision A). temporal_holdout is the latest slice by per-case sim_hour; calibration_holdout is carved from the remaining (earlier) cases; the rest is the Phase 3 training pool, from which train / model-selection-val are split at model-fit time. temporal_holdout and calibration_holdout are each materialized to their own CSV and sha256-committed to phase3_eval_lock.json, exactly like the Phase 2 eval set. train and model-selection-val are 'seen' data and are NOT hash-locked.
phase3_data_split.calibration_holdout_carve: Carved by CUSTOMER from the pool of cases with sim_hour < temporal boundary. The earlier-pool customers are shuffled with calibration_holdout_carve_seed, then added to the calibration holdout one customer at a time until the accumulated earlier-pool case count first reaches 0.15 * (all baseline seed-42 cases). All of a taken customer's earlier-pool cases are in the calibration holdout; every other customer's earlier-pool cases are the training pool. This makes training_pool and calibration_holdout exactly customer-disjoint by construction (not by a post-hoc move). Deterministic given the carve seed. Rationale: the population has ~10 cases/customer, so a case-level 15% sample would touch almost every customer and, after wholesale customer assignment, collapse the training pool -- carving by customer is the only way to get both ~15% of cases AND customer-disjointness.
phase3_data_split.customer_disjointness: enforced between {training_pool, calibration_holdout} by the wholesale-customer rule above. NOT enforced against temporal_holdout: a customer active both before and after the temporal boundary legitimately appears in both the training pool and temporal_holdout -- accepted, documented exception for the temporal gate only (Decision K).

phase3_calibration.description: In-profile calibration gate for the joint outcome model's p_recovery head. Reliability computed with sklearn.calibration.calibration_curve(n_bins=10, strategy='quantile') on candidate-level rows of the calibration_holdout slice (Decision A). HARD gate.
phase3_calibration._rationale: 0.05 per-bin reuses the same 'a gap larger than this is not trustworthy' principle already locked for the Phase 2 empirical-vs-analytic dataset check (ground_truth_treatment_effect.max_absolute_probability_gap); at the calibration_holdout size (~450 cases x ~9.6 candidates ~= 4300 rows, ~430/bin) binomial noise per bin is ~0.014 at p~0.9 and ~0.024 near p~0.5, so 0.05 is ~2-3 sigma -- tolerant of sampling noise, intolerant of real miscalibration. ECE tightened to 0.03 because it aggregates across bins and a systematic (not noisy) offset should fail even when no single bin exceeds 0.05.

phase3_treatment_effect.description: Ground-truth treatment-effect gate (Decision D -- NEW block, does NOT reuse ground_truth_treatment_effect's tolerances verbatim). Model's estimated effect = model(candidate) - model(do_nothing) for the same case, compared in probability units (p_recovery head vs the generator's analytic_p from truth_*.csv). Bucketed by the Phase-2-proven v3 keys. HARD gate; independent / time-gapped review required before sign-off (no self-certification).
phase3_treatment_effect.bucket_keys_source: reuses ground_truth_treatment_effect.bucket_keys (v3-effect-class-bucketing, locked 2026-08-31T02:41:01Z) -- Decision D concerned tolerances, not the bucketing methodology, which is independently justified and unchanged
phase3_treatment_effect.evaluation_population: training_pool UNION calibration_holdout (i.e. every baseline-seed-42 case with sim_hour < the temporal boundary) -- NOT calibration_holdout alone.
phase3_treatment_effect._rationale: Direction match is the real hard requirement (execution plan: 'in direction always'); 0.90 (not 1.0) matches Phase 2 and lets a single genuinely near-zero bucket land on the wrong side of zero without failing the phase. effect_size_floor 0.05 is kept identical to Phase 2's effect-size gate because 'is this true effect big enough for its sign to be meaningful' is a property of the generator, unchanged. max_abs_effect_gap 0.10 = 2x the Phase-2 dataset gap (0.05) because Phase 3 compounds two error sources the dataset check does not have: model estimation error at the candidate AND at the do_nothing baseline, and a single regularized shared model is known to shrink weak effects (execution plan risk table) -- 0.10 catches gross effect miscalibration while the direction test guards the shrinkage case. min_direction_scored_buckets 4 = what Phase 2 empirically produced at floor 0.05, n=3000; the Phase 3 eval harness is expected to widen candidate-space coverage and ALSO report effect direction in expected-rupee space as supporting evidence (see PHASE3_NOTES).
phase3_treatment_effect._amendment_reason: Fills a genuine gap in the original 2026-09-01T15:11:20Z lock, which specified tolerances but not the evaluation population -- BEFORE any Phase 3 evaluation has ever been run against this block (no ml/train_outcome_model.py existed yet at either timestamp), so this is completing an underspecified lock, not adjusting one after seeing a result. Reasoning: this gate needs enough cases per bucket to reach min_cases_per_bucket_for_check=100 across the ~19 buckets Phase 2 proved evaluable at n=3000 (see phase2_verify.py Section 6a / locked_thresholds ground_truth_treatment_effect). calibration_holdout alone has only 455 cases (~15% of 3000) -- restricting the gate to it would starve most of those buckets below the count floor and silently collapse statistical power exactly where the ground-truth check needs it most. training_pool UNION calibration_holdout is ~2550 cases (85% of the visible pool, everything except temporal_holdout), close enough to the n=3000 Phase 2 validated the bucketing against. This population choice does not weaken the gate: it is not 'unseen' data in the calibration/generalization sense (Decision A reserves that property for calibration_holdout and temporal_holdout specifically, used by phase3_calibration and phase3_temporal), and the treatment-effect check's own validity does not depend on held-out-ness -- it depends on comparing the model's estimated effect against the generator's known analytic effect across enough cases per bucket to make the comparison meaningful. No numeric tolerance above (min_cases_per_bucket_for_check, effect_size_floor, max_abs_effect_gap, min_fraction_buckets_matching_direction, min_direction_scored_buckets) was changed by this amendment.

phase3_cross_profile.description: Cross-calibration-profile generalization. Model trained ONLY on the baseline training pool; calibration (same metric as phase3_calibration) evaluated on the entire unseen stress-profile seed-42 dataset. Execution plan calls this the PRIMARY generalization evidence, ahead of multi-seed. HARD gate.
phase3_cross_profile._rationale: The stress profile shifts global_intercept_shift by -0.35 logit, ~4.5x incident rate, network_health_weight 0.9->1.3, fatigue penalty 0.12->0.22. A model that learned real structure should still track level and direction but WILL drift some. The gate's job (execution plan) is to distinguish 'learned structure' from 'memorized one profile's numbers', so the bar is 'still recognizably calibrated' -- ~2x the in-profile bound (0.10 / 0.07).
phase3_cross_profile._amendment_authority: Independent review decision, recorded by the reviewer after two rounds of evidence. The implementer did not make this call and is explicitly barred from re-litigating it.
phase3_cross_profile._amendment_reason: GATE REDEFINED from a raw-ECE numeric bound to a ranking-transfer criterion plus a disclosed known-limitation entry. The original max_abs_bin_gap (0.10) and max_expected_calibration_error (0.07) above are RETAINED IN THE RECORD but are NO LONGER PASS/FAIL -- they are reported as a known-limitation measurement. Justification, which predates and is independent of any desire to obtain a passing result: (i) AUC-INVARIANCE ARGUMENT. The gate's stated purpose (execution plan) is to distinguish a model that learned real structure from one that memorized one profile's specific numbers. Memorization manifests as ranking collapse on the unseen profile; ROC-AUC is invariant under ANY monotone transformation of the scores, so it isolates ordering ability from calibration level. Raw ECE conflates the two and therefore does not operationalize the gate's own stated purpose: it penalizes a model identically whether it failed to learn transferable structure or merely could not anticipate an unobservable level shift. (ii) DIRECT NULL-RESULT EXPERIMENT. On 2026-09-01 a feature change (explicit generator-cell interaction categoricals) cut temporal treatment-effect shrinkage by ~50% (slope 0.360 -> 0.543), lifted temporal ranking agreement 0.833 -> 0.891, improved in-profile calibration ECE 0.0186 -> 0.0137, and improved stress ranking AUC 0.628 -> 0.638 -- and moved cross-profile ECE by 0.0003 (0.0815 -> 0.0812) and maxgap by 0.0003 (0.1013 -> 0.1016). A change that demonstrably improved structural learning across every other axis left this metric completely flat. That is direct experimental evidence that cross-profile ECE is NOT measuring a structural-learning gap the model can close; it is measuring the stress profile's deliberately unobservable global_intercept_shift (-0.35) plus unobservable COEFFICIENT shifts (fatigue_penalty_per_contact 0.12->0.22, network_health_weight 0.9->1.3), none of which have any observable correlate in the feature set. (iii) NO VALID CORRECTED TEST EXISTS. A recalibration-protocol variant of this gate cannot currently be tested: the entire stress dataset is the locked evaluation artifact and no disjoint stress calibration sample exists (established by the provenance audit of 2026-09-01, which invalidated an earlier circular recalibration result that had fit a shift parameter on stress eval labels and scored ECE on a superset of those same rows).
phase3_cross_profile.in_profile_auc_reference: calibration_holdout (baseline profile, unseen), scored with the baseline network-health lookup; stress scored with the stress-profile network-health lookup
phase3_cross_profile.known_limitation: Raw calibration LEVEL under the stress profile is a known, disclosed limitation, not a pass/fail criterion. The stress profile carries a global_intercept_shift of -0.35 with no observable correlate, so a baseline-trained model systematically over-predicts recovery on stress data by a near-uniform offset across the whole probability range (measured: uniform +0.06..+0.10 per-decile gap, mean_pred 0.886 vs mean_actual 0.805). This is expected and is corrected in production by Phase 6+ recalibration against real observed outcomes, not by the model. The ECE/maxgap numbers are still COMPUTED AND REPORTED on every gate run so the limitation stays visible and quantified.
phase3_cross_profile._auc_tolerance_rationale: 0.05 absolute AUC degradation is ~1/3 of the in-profile above-chance discrimination signal (in-profile AUC ~0.646, i.e. ~0.146 above chance). Wide enough to absorb genuine distribution shift and finite-sample noise on the 3000-case stress set; narrow enough that a memorization collapse -- which drives AUC toward 0.5, a degradation of ~0.146 -- fails decisively. min_stress_auc_absolute 0.55 is a floor so the criterion cannot be satisfied by a model that is uninformative in BOTH profiles (which would show near-zero degradation for the wrong reason). Both numbers are derived from the structure of the discrimination signal, not from the observed stress AUC.

phase3_temporal.description: Temporal generalization on the baseline temporal_holdout (latest 15% of cases by sim_hour). Two sub-checks: (1) calibration, same metric as phase3_calibration; (2) ranking-direction preservation on constructed within-case candidate pairs. HARD gate.
phase3_temporal.ranking_pair_definition: within one holdout case, an ordered candidate pair (A, B) is eligible when the generator's analytic TREATMENT EFFECT for A (analytic_p(A) - analytic_p(do_nothing)) exceeds that for B by at least ranking_effect_size_floor (0.05); the model passes the pair when the model's estimated treatment effect for A (model_p(A) - model_p(do_nothing)) is >= that for B.
phase3_temporal._rationale: Same profile, later time window -> only mild drift expected (bank-health random walk, accumulated fatigue history), so calibration bounds sit between in-profile (0.05/0.03) and cross-profile (0.10/0.07). Ranking agreement 0.85 is what Phase 4 actually consumes; pairwise ranking on a noisy synthetic holdout is inherently noisier than aggregate calibration, so 0.85 (not 0.90+) tolerates near-tie noise while still proving the ordering is real. min 500 eligible pairs before the number is reported.
phase3_temporal._amendment_reason: Methodology correction to ranking_pair_definition, made after the FIRST evaluation run exposed the flaw but BEFORE this gate has signed off anything. Original text compared the generator's analytic *probability* treatment effect (a P difference) against the model's expected recovered *amount* (an absolute rupee expected value, p x E[amount|recovered]) -- two different quantities in two different units. That conflation injects the amount head's per-candidate variance into what is meant to be a treatment-effect ranking-direction check, and is not order-equivalent to what Phase 4 ranks by (Phase 4 ranks by EIV = expected_recovered_amount(candidate) - expected_recovered_amount(do_nothing) - cost, i.e. an effect DIFFERENCE, not a raw expected value). The corrected definition compares like-for-like: the model's probability-space treatment effect (model_p(candidate) - model_p(do_nothing)) against the generator's probability-space analytic effect. This is a real methodological flaw in the check's construction, not a threshold that turned out inconvenient -- min_ranking_direction_agreement stays at 0.85 and min_ranking_pairs at 500, both unchanged. The 0.05 floor was already referenced in the original text (as effect_size_floor_for_direction_test); it is now named explicitly as ranking_effect_size_floor so the harness reads it from config rather than hard-coding it.

phase3_multiseed.description: Supporting (secondary) robustness check -- explicitly NOT the primary generalization proof (execution plan + Phase_Acceptance_Test_Gates.md both rank cross-profile higher). Regenerate the baseline dataset at each seed, apply the identical phase3_data_split, retrain, re-run the hard gates.
phase3_multiseed.pass_criterion: phase3_calibration, phase3_treatment_effect, phase3_cross_profile and phase3_temporal all pass on every seed, AND the sign of every direction-scored phase3_treatment_effect bucket is identical across all three seeds.
phase3_multiseed._rationale: 42/43/44 per Decision F. 'Stable qualitative conclusions' (execution plan's loose phrasing) is pinned to a concrete, checkable criterion: same gate outcomes + same per-bucket effect signs across seeds. No new numeric tolerance -- it is the other blocks, re-run.

phase3_parity.description: Train/serve parity: one fixed set of representative (context, candidate) pairs scored (a) through the offline training/eval harness and (b) through ml/inference.py as Phase 4's optimizer will call it. HARD gate. Realized structurally by one shared feature-construction function and one shared model-load path imported by both sides.
phase3_parity.fallback_requires: a dated _amendment_locked_at_utc + justification if the exact-match check ever has to be relaxed to the fallback tolerance (threshold-change-audit gate)
phase3_parity.required_coverage: must include do_nothing, at least one method_change candidate, at least one null / missing network-health case, at least one row per event_type, and at least one row per root_cause_effect_class
phase3_parity._rationale: Same fitted pipeline + same deterministic feature construction -> identical output. Any non-zero difference is a real train/serve divergence bug (the exact risk this gate exists for -- execution plan risk table: 'a model trained with a feature the live serving path does not supply'), not tolerable noise, so the tolerance is 0.

phase6_experiment_assignment.description: Live experiment assignment: the randomization method, the holdout fraction, and the randomization-balance gate that decides whether any downstream incremental-Rs number is trustworthy. HARD gate. Locked at Phase 6 checkpoint X0, before assign_experiment_group.py existed and before a single opportunity had been assigned.
phase6_experiment_assignment._mirrors: backend/engine/phase6_config.py, which is the executable source of truth. This block is the dated, human-auditable record; phase6_config._check() and tests/test_phase6_config.py assert the two agree.
phase6_experiment_assignment.assignment_formula: bucket = int.from_bytes(blake2b((salt + ':' + opportunity_id).encode('utf-8'), digest_size=8).digest(), 'big') / 2**64; group = 'control' if bucket < holdout_fraction else 'treatment'
phase6_experiment_assignment._assignment_rationale: Ruling 2026-09-04: option R2, hash bucketing, over R4 stratified/blocked randomization. Independence from every covariate is STRUCTURAL rather than empirical -- opportunity_id is uuid4-derived and minted before any covariate is read, so hashing it cannot induce a correlation. Reproducible (any row's group recomputable from id + salt), stateless (correct under concurrency, unlike a seeded RNG sequence whose result depends on call order), and idempotent (a retry cannot re-randomize a live opportunity). R4 declined as premature: if the balance gate below actually fails at X5, escalating to stratification is the documented response, with that failure as its evidence.
phase6_experiment_assignment._holdout_rationale: Ruling 2026-09-04: 0.5, revised up from a proposed 0.20. Chosen for statistical power, not demo realism. The usual reason to keep a holdout small -- every control opportunity is revenue deliberately left unrecovered -- does not apply to a synthetic system where no real money is sacrificed. Against the reconciled seeded population (150 opportunities, of which 51 are already terminal, 92 in flight, 7 escalated-pending), an even split is the only allocation giving the balance gate a usable control arm at achievable volume.
phase6_experiment_assignment._min_assigned_n_rationale: Below this the gate reports its raw numbers but returns NOT_EVALUABLE rather than PASS. Refusing to certify balance on a sample too small to detect imbalance is the entire point of the gate.
phase6_experiment_assignment._min_assigned_n_amendment_reason: AMENDED at X5 from 200 to 3500. The original was set without a power analysis and was mutually incompatible with max_abs_smd = 0.10, locked at the same moment: SE(SMD) is roughly 2/sqrt(n), so at n=240 each level's SMD has SD about 0.13 while the gate takes the maximum over ten such quantities against a 0.10 bound. Measured under the true-random null using the real locked hash, seeded and reproducible (backend/analytics/balance_power_analysis.py): pass rate / 95% Wilson lower bound is 0.33% / 0.09% at n=240 (2 of 600 trials), 8.17% / 6.23% at n=500, 34.67% / 30.97% at n=1000, 60.33% / 56.37% at n=1500, 77.50% / 73.99% at n=2000, 88.00% / 86.50% at n=2500, 93.75% / 92.60% at n=3000, 97.00% / 96.16% at n=3500, 98.75% / 98.16% at n=4000, 99.25% / 98.77% at n=4500 (2000 trials at each of the last five). A correct randomizer fails this gate 99.67% of the time at n=240, so those failures carried no information about the randomizer -- exactly the diagnosis-independent-of-the-failing-result standard this file requires for an amendment. NOTE ON THE TRIAL COUNT: a first pass at 500 trials put n=3500 at 98.0% and a second at 96.0%, straddling the criterion and moving the chosen floor between runs, because _draw_rows minted ids with uuid.uuid4() which ignores the seed. A locked threshold justified by an unreproducible measurement is not justified; id generation is now seeded and the estimate is stable to repeat runs. CRITICALLY, max_abs_smd is UNCHANGED at 0.10 -- the bound that judges the result is exactly what it was before any result was seen. What moved is the precondition for evaluating the gate at all, and it moved in the CONSERVATIVE direction: more evidence is now required before balance may be certified, not less. 3500 is the smallest n on the measured curve whose 95% Wilson LOWER bound clears a 95% pass rate (98.0% observed, 96.4% lower); the lower bound rather than the point estimate because a Monte Carlo pass rate is itself an estimate and choosing on the point estimate would clear the criterion by sampling luck about half the time. n=3000 does not clear it (94.4% observed, 92.0% lower). Full curve recorded in backend/PHASE6_NOTES.md.
phase6_experiment_assignment._min_assigned_n_detection_check: The 95% criterion controls the FALSE-FAILURE rate only, so the same module measures the other side: how often the gate fires on an assigner that IS biased. At n=3500, 300 trials, reported against the imbalance each bias actually induces -- induced |SMD| 0.0130 (below bound) 3.7% detection, which is the null rate; 0.0827 (below) 36.3%; 0.1312 (ABOVE) 80.0%; 0.1743 (ABOVE) 99.7%; 0.2671 (ABOVE) 100.0%. Detection near the null rate BELOW the bound is correct behaviour and not a blind spot: a gate firing there would enforce a tighter threshold than the one locked. Above the bound it rises sharply and saturates. NOTE ON READING THIS: an earlier pass at this curve was parameterised by the raw bias knob (probability units) rather than by induced SMD (the gate's units) and wrongly concluded the gate was insensitive -- a 0.05 bias induces only ~0.042 SMD and a 0.10 bias ~0.086, both below the 0.10 the gate is told to enforce. The curve is now reported in induced-SMD units so it cannot be misread the same way.
phase6_experiment_assignment._min_assigned_n_known_limitation: Only the definition of the bound itself: an imbalance smaller than 0.10 SMD passes by construction, so a PASS means 'no imbalance beyond the declared tolerance', never 'the arms are identical'.
phase6_experiment_assignment._smd_bound_rationale: The covariate-balance convention: SMD < 0.10 is negligible imbalance. This is NOT Cohen's 0.20, which is a small-EFFECT-SIZE convention for a different construct. An earlier draft of this plan proposed 0.20 by conflating the two; the error was diagnosed and corrected on 2026-09-04 BEFORE anything was locked and before any balance result had been computed, so this is a pre-lock correction and not a threshold moved to obtain a pass.
phase6_experiment_assignment.continuous_smd_formula: (mean_t - mean_c) / sqrt((s_t^2 + s_c^2) / 2), s = sample standard deviation with ddof=1

diagnosis._rationale: Replaces a root_cause covariate carrying a NULL level. Verified 2026-09-04 against the seeded population: root_cause IS NULL exactly when event_type != 'payment_failed' (54 checkout_abandoned + 32 invoice_overdue = 86 of 150, zero exceptions). A NULL level is therefore perfectly collinear with event_type, and lumping 86 rows into it would be blind to a checkout_abandoned/invoice_overdue split -- an imbalance this 8-level form detects and the 7-level form scores as exactly 0.

is_payment_failed._rationale: NOT redundant with diagnosis, and the one deliberate overlap between covariates. Per-level balance on a partition does not imply balance on a coarsening of it: six root-cause levels each off by +0.03 in the same direction every one clear the 0.10 bound individually while their union is off by 0.18. diagnosis cannot see that; this binary can. The two GENUINELY redundant levels of the original event_type covariate -- checkout_abandoned and invoice_overdue, identical partitions in both covariates -- were dropped rather than gated twice.

phase6_experiment_assignment.categorical_smd_formula: per level k, with p the within-arm proportion of that level: (p_t - p_c) / sqrt((p_t(1 - p_t) + p_c(1 - p_c)) / 2)
phase6_experiment_assignment.categorical_gate: max over gate-eligible levels of |SMD_k| < max_abs_smd. Identical to requiring every eligible level to clear it -- max < x and forall < x are the same proposition at every n, by the definition of max. No multiplicity correction applies: SMD is a descriptive bound, not a hypothesis test, so there is no family-wise error rate to inflate.

degenerate_smd_convention._rationale: The denominator vanishes only when both arms' proportions are 0 or 1. Both cases get an explicit value rather than a ZeroDivisionError or a silent nan, which would compare False against every bound and pass. A level present in one arm and absent from the other is maximal imbalance and must fail, never be swallowed as 'undefined'.

phase6_experiment_assignment.level_eligibility_rule: a categorical level enters the gate only when min(h, 1 - h) * n_level >= min_expected_arm_count, with h = holdout_fraction and n_level the level's total across both arms
phase6_experiment_assignment._eligibility_rationale: The classic >=5 expected-cell-count rule, applied to the arm that actually drives the estimate's noise. Written holdout-aware rather than as a raw count so it stays correct if holdout_fraction is ever amended.
phase6_experiment_assignment.excluded_level_handling: each excluded level is reported with its raw per-arm counts and labelled EXCLUDED_UNDERPOWERED; if excluded levels together cover more than max_excluded_coverage of the assigned population the gate reports NOT_EVALUABLE, never PASS
phase6_experiment_assignment._coverage_guard_rationale: Without this, exclusion becomes a way to manufacture a pass: clear the two largest levels, drop the other six as underpowered, declare balance.
phase6_experiment_assignment.reporting_requirement: The gate reports RAW NUMBERS, never a bare verdict: n per arm, mean/median/sd of amount_at_risk per arm, the full level x arm contingency table, and every level's signed SMD including excluded ones. The verdict is derived from those figures in the report and never substituted for them.

phase7_incremental_attribution.description: The estimator floor for aggregate incremental attribution. HARD gate: below it the module reports 'insufficient data' and no number at all.
phase7_incremental_attribution._mirrors: backend/analytics/incremental_attribution.py MIN_N_PER_ARM; tests/test_phase7_attribution.py asserts the two agree.
phase7_incremental_attribution._rationale: 30 per arm is the conventional floor at which the normal approximation behind the Wald interval is defensible at all. Below it a confidence interval is not a weak result but a misleading one -- wide enough to contain anything while still looking like a measurement.
phase7_incremental_attribution._deliberately_not_tied_to: phase6_experiment_assignment.min_assigned_n (3500). Those floors answer different questions: 3500 is what the BALANCE gate needs to detect imbalance against a 0.10 SMD bound, 30 is what the ESTIMATOR needs for its interval to mean anything. Tying them would make one move silently with the other.
phase7_incremental_attribution._LOCKED_LATE__DISCLOSURE: This value does NOT have the same evidentiary provenance as max_abs_smd, and that is stated rather than implied. max_abs_smd was locked at commit 6b6409e on 2026-09-04, a day and five checkpoints before the X5 evaluation it judged. min_n_per_arm was introduced in commit 48e3810 on 2026-09-05 -- the SAME commit as the evaluation that used it. It was in fact written before that evaluation ran, but nothing in the repository can verify that ordering, and under this project's own discipline an unverifiable lock is an unlocked one. It is therefore locked HERE, dated 2026-09-05, retrospectively and openly. The current result is unaffected: the evaluated population is n=1742 treatment / 1758 control, both clearing 30 by roughly 58x, so no value of this floor anywhere between 30 and ~1700 would change the reported outcome. Any FUTURE evaluation is judged against this dated lock.
phase7_incremental_attribution.estimator: difference in proportions with a Wald 95% interval (rate); difference in means with a Welch unpooled-variance 95% interval (rupees)
phase7_incremental_attribution.reporting_requirement: Every reported figure carries its confidence interval, the population it is averaged over, and an explicit synthetic label. A point estimate without its interval is a claim the data may not support.

phase6_counterfactual_consistency.description: Control suppression is verifiably real rather than cosmetic. HARD gate. Locked at X0, before the suppression code existed.
control_probes: recovery_executions.state IN ('dispatched','executed') at or after assigned_at
phase6_counterfactual_consistency._rationale: Every probe count is reported raw. The gate requires all-zero on the control arm AND non-zero on the treatment arm: without the second half 'control shows nothing' is unfalsifiable, since a system that acts on nobody at all would pass it.
phase6_counterfactual_consistency.reporting_requirement: raw per-probe counts for both arms, never a bare verdict
